report.scope: US market, home robot vacuums and vacuum-mop combos, from basic bots to full-dock flagships. Prices seen Nov 6–13, 2026, during early Black Friday sales.

primer.what_it_is: A small robot that vacuums (and often mops) your floors on a schedule, then returns to its dock to charge.

must_haves.why: A spinning laser maps your home so the robot cleans in rows, not random bumps.
Clean the kitchen after dinner without running the whole house.
Brushes, filters and pads are a recurring cost for years.

premium_features.why: Empties the bin for you; you touch it every few weeks.
Washes and dries the mop and refills water; worth it with lots of hard floor.
Dodges cords, socks and pet mess.

avoid.why: They bump around randomly and miss spots.
Robot vacuums are discounted 30–50% several times a year.
Robots depend on apps and parts for years.

verdict.headline: Buy a mid-range mop-washing dock during early Black Friday; flagships add little for most homes.
verdict.confidence: Moderate: current prices seen for 10 models; four flagship and older-model prices are estimates.
verdict.reasoning: Counting purchase price over about four years plus parts, a $230 LiDAR bot costs ~$87 a year and a full mop-washing dock ~$215–$290. Cleaning gains flatten above the mid-range full dock; flagships at $1,000–$1,600 mostly add obstacle avoidance and arms.
verdict.price_watch_summary: The Eufy Omni C28 is $459.99 (down from $799.99) right now; buy at $460 or less.

recommendation.why: A full mop-washing, self-emptying dock at a mid-range price; early Black Friday already reached the strike price.

normalization.unit: Cost per year of ownership: purchase price ÷ expected years of service, plus yearly parts
normalization.unit_rationale: Sticker price ignores that docks need bags, pads and cleaning solution, and that cheap bots die sooner. Cost per year puts a $230 bot and a $1,600 flagship on the same scale.
normalization.quality_adjustment: Expected life: about 3 years for basic bots, 4 for mainstream LiDAR models, 5 for flagships. Yearly parts: about $25–$30 for vacuum-only, $60 with a self-empty dock (bags), $100–$120 with a mop-washing dock (pads, solution, bags). These are estimates from owner and maintenance guides.
normalization.formula: Cost per year = price ÷ expected years + yearly parts

bands.label: Premium
bands.verdict: Upper mid-range or last year's flagship

normalization.size_economics: No bulk angle; the lever is timing. Last year's flagship often sells for half its launch price when the new one arrives.

diminishing_returns.knee_example: Eufy Omni C28 at $459.99: full mop-washing dock for ~$215 a year
diminishing_returns.below_knee: Below ~$130 a year you give up the self-empty dock, and below ~$85 you lose LiDAR maps.
diminishing_returns.above_knee: Above ~$290 a year you pay for camera avoidance, extending arms and top suction ratings, which most homes rarely notice.

best_budget.why: LiDAR maps and room control for $229.99.

best_premium.why: Last year's flagship with camera avoidance at about $800.

best_for_beginners.why: Self-emptying with LiDAR for about $280; simple and low-effort.

longest_lasting.why: Roborock's parts availability and app track record favor a long life.

consensus.expert_view: Reviewers split on the top pick (Dreame X60 Max Ultra, Shark PowerDetect, Eufy X10 Pro Omni) but agree LiDAR and a good dock matter more than peak suction.
consensus.community_view: Owners favor Roborock for reliability, expect 3–5 years of life with basic care, and warn about the steady cost of brushes, filters and pads.
consensus.where_they_disagree: Experts rank flagships highest; owners often say a mid-range model with a good dock covers what they need.

deal_intelligence.volatility: Very high: prices swing 30–50% between list and sales, and models turn over yearly.
deal_intelligence.best_time_to_buy: Now through Cyber Monday (Nov 30); Prime Day in July is the next big chance.
deal_intelligence.patience_payoff: Some models dip lower in spring (X10 Pro Omni hit $479.99), but early Black Friday prices are already near their lows.
deal_intelligence.discount_honesty: List prices are inflated; judge deals against the last sale price, not the 'was' price.

price_segments.why: What the dock does (nothing, empties the bin, or also washes the mop) sets the price band more than brand does.

segments.label: Vacuum only
segments.what_you_get: A robot that vacuums on a schedule; LiDAR models map rooms.
segments.watch_out: Skip non-LiDAR bots; LiDAR costs only ~$60 more.

segments.label: Self-emptying
segments.what_you_get: A dock that empties the bin, so you touch it every few weeks, not every run.
segments.watch_out: Bags add ~$30 a year; list prices are inflated, so buy on sale.

segments.label: Mop-washing dock
segments.what_you_get: A dock that also washes and dries the mop and refills water: real hands-off mopping.
segments.watch_out: Consumables run ~$100 a year; worth it only with lots of hard floor.

segments.label: Flagship
segments.what_you_get: Best obstacle avoidance, extending arms, top suction.
segments.watch_out: Last year's flagship often costs half; this year's adds little for most homes.
